ratelimit -- census of the 62 VERIFIED kernel calls (the mainstage call of each
case; the driver calls the body four times per case -- evalstage, warmupstage,
mainstage, then one post-verification timing call -- and only the third decides
the verdict).

Produced by evidence/ratelimit/ratelimit.census-probe.cpp, which is the SHIPPED
translation plus one fprintf to stderr and changes no compared output: the run
it came from is GREEN at 62 of 62 with 14,818 IDENTICAL rows
(kernel.census-probe.run.txt). So this is a reading of the captured corpus, not
a perturbation of it -- unit #34's clamp_census shape.

`inst` is printed as the value on ENTRY (the probe prints *inst-1 after the
increment). `raw` is the unsaturated rate, before saturate_c.

  RESET 3   UPPER-clamped 20   LOWER-clamped 19   interior 20

THE THREE RESET CASES CARRY NOTHING BUT ZEROS. in, last, rv and out are all
exactly 0 on invocations 1, 2 and 3, so the THEN arm and the ELSE arm compute
the same answer there:

    THEN:  ResetValue_ = rv = 0            -> returns 0, stores 0
    ELSE:  raw = (0 - 0)/DT = 0            -> returns 0 + saturate(0)*DT = 0

That is why BOTH the reset-arm stub and the ignores-ResetValue stub pass 62 of
62. It is a property of the captured inputs, not of the instrument.
